model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management FY2027-FY2030 EPRA EPS guidance (c.5% CAGR to c.62p, ~80% from the existing portfolio) haircut to 4.5%; the historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward proxy -- see notes.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (book) CAGR of -1.9%/-2.3% diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (+7.0%/+4.1%) and EPRA EPS (+8.7%/-1.1%). This is expected for an IAS 40 REIT: book value is the mark-to-market of the portfolio (NTA/share fell from 1,348p FY2019 to 882p FY2026 on cap-rate expansion), not retained earnings, so the equity CAGR says nothing about the income stream being capitalised. Do not use it for growth selection.
historical_growth.notes: EPS and FCF rows are the EPRA series (EPRA EPS in pence; 'fcf' = EPRA earnings GBP m), not the statutory EPS/FCF, which are revaluation-driven and sign-flipping. The 5-year CAGRs start from the FY2021 Covid trough (EPRA EPS 33.9p, earnings 251m) and so flatter the trend; the 3-year CAGRs from the FY2023 post-recovery peak (53.1p) are slightly negative because GBP 1.3bn of FY2023 disposals, the FY2025-26 QAM finance-lease sale and higher finance costs (84m -> 124m) absorbed the 4-5% like-for-like rental growth. SBC is immaterial (GBP 2-9m) and inside EPRA earnings, so there is no SBC-adjusted vs reported gap to report.

scenario_narratives.base: Management delivers the guided path: FY2027 EPRA EPS stable at 51.4p as the QAM/disposal drag offsets 3-5% like-for-like rental growth, FY2028 high-single-digit growth as the London office pipeline lets up, and c.62p by FY2030 (c.5% CAGR) with ~80% coming from the existing platform. Overheads stay in the low GBP 60m's, net debt/EBITDA falls below 7x by FY2028 without further material disposals, and the dividend grows in line at 1.2-1.3x cover. Growth fades to 2.5% and the stream is capitalised at a 9% cost of equity with 2% terminal growth -- no NTA-discount closure is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prime-location scarcity does its work: build costs ~2x existing book value keep new supply out, rental growth stays at two-decade highs, the GBP 1bn retail recycling lands at the targeted 200bps income pick-up, and AI/tech demand keeps prime London offices full. EPRA EPS reaches c.66p by FY2030, 6% above target, the 2028-30 refinancing comes in at or below today's 3.6% as gilts ease, and the cost of equity compresses to 8.5% with 2.5% terminal growth. The NTA discount narrows toward 10-15% as a consequence, not an input.
scenario_narratives.bear: UK macro and fiscal uncertainty bite: consumer spending stalls, retail tenant failures rise, hybrid-work and AI-driven headcount shifts finally reach prime offices, and the development pipeline lets up slowly. FY2027 EPRA EPS falls c.4.5% to 49p (guidance missed) and stays near 50p through FY2030 as the 2028+ refinancing at 5%+ and heavier compliance/leasing capex (14% of revenue) absorb the modest rental growth. Leverage at 8.4x net debt/EBITDA and 38.7% LTV magnifies the hit: the cost of equity rises to 10% and terminal growth falls to 1.5%. Covenants (65% LTV, 1.45x ICR) are not threatened -- this is an earnings-stagnation bear, not a solvency bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Landsec is valued on the income it actually distributes, not on NAV: EPRA earnings less a maintenance/leasing capex charge (AFFO), projected on management's guided EPS path and capitalised at a GBP cost of equity with net debt held at zero because the flow is already post-interest. EPRA NTA of 882p is a cross-check, not the model -- the c.25% discount the base value shows to NTA is what a 9% cost of equity does to an 8.5% earnings yield growing at 2-3%, and it will close only if rates fall or the income grows faster than guided (the bull case). Statutory net income, P/E, EV/EBITDA and reported FCF are all meaningless for this company and are not used.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 9% base moves the base value by roughly 7-8%; a gilt back-up is the single largest risk to both the model and the market price
FY2028 'high single digit' EPS growth depends on the ~GBP 1bn London office programme letting up within ~12 months of completion; a slow lease-up pushes the whole path right by a year
The 2028+ debt maturities (average cost 3.6% today, 89% hedged) will reprice; the base holds the margin flat after FY2030 and does not model a refinancing benefit or penalty
Maintenance capex sizing (11% of revenue vs FY2026 actual 16%): if the net-zero/EPC and repositioning spend proves permanent, the bear's 14% is the better base and the value is c.8% lower

Capital recycling execution: FY2026 disposals crystallised a GBP 104m loss on investment properties against book; the retail acquisition programme must land at the targeted 200bps pick-up for the growth path to hold
UK REIT tax regime change would convert a 0% cash tax rate into a ~25% one and is not in any scenario

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (LSE regular close); 52-week range 525-726p
data_sources.financials: LAND.L_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (EPRA revenue/operating profit/earnings/EPS, NTA per share, net debt, LTV, capex split) from the FY2019-FY2026 annual reports; FY2026 annual report notes for the diluted share count (line 7348), net debt (line 8748), EPRA capex analysis (table 62, line 10240) and the FY2027-FY2030 guidance (lines 299-316, 1264-1367)
data_sources.qualitative: LAND.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, moat, risks, guidance table and sell-side range (670-780p)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 EPRA revenue (kpis EPRARevenue; statutory revenue 892 includes trading-property sales and development-management fees). This is the driver line; the engine's 'EBITDA margin' is the EPRA-earnings margin on it.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average 747m per FY2026 annual report note (line 7348: basic 743m, diluted 747m). Held flat: FY2026 buyback was only GBP 27m (scrip-dilution offset), share-based payments are expensed inside EPRA earnings, and no equity raise is signalled (LTV 38.7% falling, no refinancing before 2028).
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by the REIT-row rule: EPRA earnings are already after net finance expense (GBP 124m FY2026), so capitalising them at the cost of equity and then deducting net debt would charge the debt twice. Actual 31-Mar-2026 net debt was GBP 4,234m reported / GBP 4,210m adjusted (FY2026 AR line 8748), gross borrowings GBP 4,360m, cash GBP 106m, LTV 38.7%, net debt/EBITDA 8.4x. Leverage is priced through the cost of equity and the bear case, not the bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 AFFO = EPRA earnings 382 less maintenance/leasing capex charge 94.6 (11.0% of EPRA revenue). This is the owner flow the engine capitalises.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 EPRA earnings (51.4p x 743m basic). Statutory FCF (-231) is meaningless here: it is after GBP 298m of development capex and GBP 84m of acquisitions, before GBP 734m of disposal proceeds.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR cash-flow statement, share-based payments GBP 9m (CSV StockBasedComp). Set to 0 in the flows because the IFRS 2 charge sits inside overheads and is therefore already deducted in EPRA earnings; charging it again would double-count. Finance income (GBP 14m) likewise stays inside EPRA earnings as it nets against finance expense on the same balance sheet.
inputs.fx_note: Filings in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quoted pence/share (1 GBP = 100 GBp, fixed by definition, no date or source needed). No dual listing to parity-check.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:00:02Z LSE regular close (Yahoo chart API); 52-week range 525-726p
inputs.wacc_rationale: This is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. Built in GBP: 10-year gilt c.4.5-4.7% (Oct-2026), UK equity risk premium 5.0%, beta c.0.9 for a prime, AA/A+-rated UK REIT with 8.6-year debt maturity and 89% fixed/hedged -> 9.0% base. Bull 8.5% (rates easing, prime-property risk premium compressing), bear 10.0% (gilt back-up, UK fiscal/macro risk flagged high in the Analysis). Cross-check: at 604p the stock yields 6.8% on the 41.2p dividend and 8.5% on EPRA EPS; CoE 9% less 2% growth = 7% AFFO yield is consistent with the sector trading at a 20-30% NTA discount.
inputs.lease_treatment: Head-lease liabilities (GBP 997m, FY2026 AR line 9092) are the ground rents on leasehold investment properties; the related interest is inside net finance expense and therefore already deducted in EPRA earnings. No further lease charge in the flows, no lease debt in the bridge (net debt is zero anyway).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is the Liverpool ONE minority (GBP 1m share of profit FY2026, immaterial). EPRA earnings and EPRA EPS are already attributable to parent shareholders, so no NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md REIT row (IAS 40 fair-value property investor; statutory net income is revaluation and disposal noise -- FY2019-FY2026 net income swings from -1,393 to +869 on a GBP 10.8bn portfolio; EBITDA is not defined in the CSV; reported FCF is after growth development capex). Run on the Drivers/engine route per the GPT.AX and CHC.AX precedents so the dashboard sliders reproduce it. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = EPRA revenue; EBITDA margin = EPRA earnings / EPRA revenue (post net finance expense, post the de minimis REIT tax charge, post IFRS 2); D&A = 0 (investment property is not depreciated; the GBP 2m PP&E charge is inside EPRA earnings); SBC = 0 (inside EPRA earnings); cash tax = 0 (UK REIT regime, FY2026 tax charge nil on the property rental business); capex = maintenance and leasing capex, the EPRA-earnings-to-AFFO bridge; working capital = 0; net debt = 0; discount rate = cost of equity. FIRST VALUATION of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the 9-Oct-2026 LSE regular close, not an after-hours print. Balance sheet, net debt and share count are from the 31-Mar-2026 annual report -- the latest filing; the H1 FY2027 interim (to 30-Sep-2026) is due mid-November 2026 and should trigger an anchor refresh. NTA CROSS-CHECK: EPRA NTA 882p/share at 31-Mar-2026; the base value sits at a c.25% discount to NTA, which is where the capitalised income stream lands when the EPRA EPS yield (8.5% at 604p) exceeds the cost of equity less growth -- the discount is an income-yield fact, not an input.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2027 -3%: disposal/QAM drag lands in full while like-for-like slips to the bottom of the range as weak UK consumer spending hits retail tenants and hybrid-work/AI headcount effects reach even prime offices. Thereafter 1.5% -- sub-inflation rental growth, the office pipeline lets up slowly, and the retail acquisitions are deferred because the share price (wide NTA discount) and leverage (8.4x ND/EBITDA) make capital expensive.
bear.margin_rationale: FY2027 49.1p (-4.5% -- guidance missed), then margin compresses to 43% by FY2030 as the 2028+ maturities refinance at c.5%+ (average cost 3.6% today, 89% hedged only until the hedges roll), the FY2027 GBP 6-8m empty-development interest drag persists, and bad-debt provisions normalise upward. EPRA EPS stuck at c.50p through FY2030.
bear.capex_rationale: Maintenance/leasing capex at 14% of revenue (GBP 120m, close to the FY2026 actual GBP 140m): tighter MEES/EPC-B thresholds, Building Safety Act compliance and heavier leasing incentives to hold occupancy are all recurring, not one-off.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.0% / 1.5% = 11.9x terminal AFFO (8.4% yield): a renewed gilt back-up re-widens the UK REIT risk premium.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 EPRA revenue -1%: like-for-like net rental income +3-5% (guided) is offset by the lost QAM finance-lease income and the income on GBP 705m of FY2026 disposals (retail parks at 6.4%, offices at 4.9%). FY2028 +4% as the c.GBP 1bn London office programme (Timber Square, Thirty High) lets up within ~12 months of completion. FY2029-31 +3.5% on reversion capture (relettings/renewals +15%, two-decade-high occupancy 98%) and up to GBP 1bn of retail acquisitions at a ~200bps income-return pick-up over the offices sold. Fades to 2.5% by FY2034 -- indexed/reviewed prime rents, no cap-rate-driven re-rating assumed.
base.margin_rationale: EPRA earnings / EPRA revenue (FY2026 actual 44.4%, FY2025 46.9%, FY2024 48.4%). Path is set to reproduce guidance on the flat 747m share count: FY2027 45.1% -> 384m = 51.4p (stable, as guided); FY2028 46.9% -> 415m = 55.6p (+8%, 'high single digit'); FY2029 47.6% -> 436m = 58.4p; FY2030 48.8% -> 463m = 62.0p (the c.62p target). Margin expansion comes from overheads held in the low GBP 60m's while income grows, and from the GBP 6-8m FY2027 interest drag on completed-but-unlet developments reversing as they let. Held flat after FY2030: no refinancing benefit assumed when the 2028+ maturities reprice.
base.capex_rationale: Maintenance and leasing capex (the EPRA-earnings-to-AFFO bridge) at 11.0% of EPRA revenue = GBP 95m on FY2026. FY2026 EPRA capex table 62 shows GBP 117m 'no incremental lettable space' + GBP 23m tenant improvements = GBP 140m combined, but FY2019-22 ran at GBP 41-47m and the FY2023-26 step-up (102-163m) carries the net-zero/EPC programme and Myo/retail repositioning that is partly growth capex already paid for by the rental-growth path. GBP 95m is the midpoint and matches the 1.2-1.3x dividend-cover policy (EPRA earnings 382 less dividends 303 = GBP 79m retained, plus the GBP 27m buyback). Gives FY2026 AFFO 287m / 38.5p, 0.93x the 41.2p dividend -- the dividend is covered by EPRA earnings but the capex is funded from recycling, which is exactly the gap this charge captures.
base.tax_rationale: UK REIT: property rental business income is exempt; FY2026 group tax charge nil on EPRA earnings. The residual taxable (non-REIT) activity is immaterial.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 2.0% = 14.6x terminal AFFO (6.9% AFFO yield) binds well below the 18x cap. 2.0% terminal is UK CPI-ish rental indexation less obsolescence; it is below the 2.5% used on the Australian REITs because UK office carries structural hybrid-work risk and the portfolio is 50% office.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2027 flat revenue: like-for-like at the top of the 3-5% range fully absorbs the disposal/QAM drag. FY2028 +5% on faster office lease-up and the Silverburn-style retail acquisitions landing early; 4-4.5% through FY2031 as the GBP 1bn retail programme compounds the 'fewer, bigger, better stores' concentration (85% of retail in the UK top-1% destinations, rental growth fastest in ~20 years) and AI/tech office demand (+136% active requirements) keeps prime London 99% let. Fades to 3%.
bull.margin_rationale: FY2027 52.2p (+1.5%, above 'stable'); FY2028 57.4p (+10%); FY2030 66.0p, c.6% above the 62p target, on the retail-acquisition income pick-up and overheads flat in nominal terms. Then 50.5% held: the 2028-30 refinancing happens at or below the 3.6% average cost as gilts ease.
bull.capex_rationale: Maintenance/leasing capex eases to 9.5% of revenue as the net-zero/EPC catch-up completes and the newly built office stock needs little refurbishment for a decade.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.5% / 2.5% = 17.1x terminal AFFO, still inside the 18x cap.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. The bear weight is raised to 25% because the Analysis rates UK macro/fiscal risk 'high' and interest-rate sensitivity 'moderate-high', and 8.4x net debt/EBITDA means a cap-rate or refinancing shock reaches equity quickly; the bull weight is held to 25% because the upside case requires both guidance beats and a lower cost of equity, and management's own 62p target already embeds the office lease-up. The balance sheet (AA/A+, 8.6-year maturity, no refinancing before 2028) is why the bear is earnings-stagnation rather than distress, which is what keeps it at 25% and not higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
